answer: Sybil resistance can hinge on a costly identity ledger: each agent must bond stake to a public key, and that key earns a unique pigment derived from its bond history. Forging many sock-puppet identities means funding each bond separately, so attacker cost scales linearly with fake agents. Peers only attest to keys whose stake sits on the shared ledge of verified history, and duplicate or recycled keys fall like sediment into the river of rejected claims, making mass identity creation economically unrewarding.
